recommendation: Keep the audit commit as a human-review marker. Ask the responsible work group and Extension Pack maintainers to confirm whether dosage-minimumGapBetweenDose should remain the current complex extension, be corrected to a simple Duration extension matching FHIR-35901, or be superseded by a newer Dosage/DosageSafety design. Do not add a core Dosage.minimumGapBetweenDose element unless that review reopens the issue for current core.
issue_request: FHIR-35901 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It asked how PCA pump lockout intervals should be represented, concluded maxDosePerPeriod should support multiple limits, and proposed a new Dosage.minimumGapBetweenDose Duration element with short text "Time that must pass between doses", definition "The minimum amount of time that must pass between administering the specified dose amount", and synonym "lockout interval".
initial_application: The Jira comments say the base change missed the R5 deadline and that an extension would be created instead. The implementation trail is Extension Pack commit 9bf87c1410aae87779e90336478f8777f618321c, which added input/definitions/datatypes/StructureDefinition-dosage-minimumGapBetweenDose.xml. Current core source retains an OID registry entry for that canonical URL and later Dosage/DosageSafety work gives dose limits a repeatable structure, but the minimum-gap extension definition itself is no longer a build-scope core source file.
additional_context: Pharmacy May 2022 WGM minutes record PCA modeling questions including PCA dose, lockout, continuous rate, and max dose per period, and FHIR-I minutes on 2023-02-15 record the Persuasive with Mod vote. Later FHIR-51540 work reworked Dosage and dose limits for R6, but that issue is still Resolved - change required and was not a separate applied/published decision for this run. The current Extension Pack artifact is present, but its differential is a complex extension with meetGoal, whenTrigger, and precondition slices and Extension.value[x] max 0 rather than a straightforward valueDuration.
reconciliation: No core source was changed. The only concrete lockout implementation is maintained in the FHIR Extension Pack outside this checkout, and changing current core Dosage source to add a base element would conflict with the documented R5 extension workaround and later Dosage refactoring without a fresh work-group decision.

related_jiras.note: Later R6 Dosage/DosageSafety refactoring affects max dose modeling but is Resolved - change required, so it was treated as context rather than decided here.
